panels.title: Merging health — is the pipe up and winning?
Merging enabled (relay)
panels.description: Admin kill switch. 0 means a merged-block simulation failed and merging was disabled.

panels.title: Relay sees builder
panels.description: Relay-side merging TCP handshake state.

panels.title: Builder sees relay
panels.description: Builder-side merging TCP handshake state.

panels.title: Merged header served
panels.description: Share of get_header calls that served the merged bid instead of the original.

panels.title: Builder servable win
panels.description: Builder's own view: emissions that beat the base builder's latest bid and were inside the relay's staleness gate.

panels.title: Merged blocks accepted
panels.description: Merged blocks per second the relay accepted from the builder.

panels.title: get_header decision mix
panels.description: Why each get_header did or did not serve a merged bid. `no_block_for_builder` means the winning builder's coinbase had no merge; `stale` means max_merged_bid_age_ms was binding.

panels.title: Merged bid margin over the original bid
panels.description: Merged value minus original bid value at get_header. The `behind` distribution is the base builder's own ratchet that the merge failed to beat.

panels.title: 1. Relay to builder — forwarding and activation
Base block forwarding outcomes
panels.description: Every decoded submission the merging tile saw, by what happened to it.

panels.title: Activation outcomes
panels.description: Top-bid updates and what the tile did with them. `not_appendable` is a builder that opted out; `not_forwarded` is a block we never sent.

panels.title: Top bid update gap
panels.description: Time between consecutive top-bid updates reaching the tile. This is the cadence the merge has to out-run.

panels.title: Appendable base blocks per slot
panels.description: Distinct blocks forwarded as merge bases in a slot. Only builders with collateral and allow_appending count.

panels.title: Merge orders declared
panels.description: Orders offered to the builder, and those dropped for an out-of-range tx index.

panels.title: Transaction wire economy
panels.description: Txs sent whole against those sent as a hash reference. A falling reference share means the dehydration cache is being reset.

panels.title: 2. Builder ingest — what arrives and what it refuses
Frames accepted from the relay
panels.description: Control and payload frames the builder took off the wire.

panels.title: Rejects sent to the relay
panels.description: Reject and fatal frames by code. `invalid_payment` here killed merging once before; watch it.

panels.title: Rejects seen by the relay
panels.description: The same refusals from the relay's side of the link. A gap against the builder panel means frames are being lost.

panels.title: Internal queue drops
panels.description: Work the builder dropped because an internal queue was full. Any sustained value here is lost merges.

panels.title: Ingest and merge-cycle rejections
panels.description: Why the builder refused a forwarded block or an emission, by stage.

panels.title: Relay activation as the builder saw it
panels.description: `advisory` is an activation for a base we hold; `unknown_base_block` means the relay activated a block we never stored.

panels.title: Merge pool size at slot end
panels.description: Base blocks, orders and builders pooled when the slot tore down.

panels.title: 3. The win condition — appended value against the base builder's own ratchet
Delta on base
panels.description: Value the merge appends. `first_pass` is what one pass on a fresh base reaches; `previous_final` is what the base we just left had accumulated. First pass below previous final means rebasing is costing us.

panels.title: Beats the base builder's own bid
panels.description: Whether the merged block beat the base builder's latest bid, and its best bid of the slot. This is the win condition itself.

targets.expr: sum by (reference) (rate(helix_builder_merge_beats_own_bid_total{job=~"$builder_job", instance=~"$builder_instance", result="yes"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (reference) (rate(helix_builder_merge_beats_own_bid_total{job=~"$builder_job", instance=~"$builder_instance"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.0001)

panels.title: Base builder bid ratchet
panels.description: How much the base builder's own bid moves between submissions. This is the value drift the merge has to out-run, not elapsed time.

panels.title: Base builder ratchet interval
panels.description: Time between a base builder's consecutive submissions. With the ratchet size, this sets the value budget a merge has.

panels.title: Why a stream gave up its base
panels.description: `base_gain_wins` means the base builder's fresh bid beat the delta we were holding. `holding` means we kept extending.

panels.title: Extend passes per base
panels.description: Improvement passes made on one base before rebasing. One pass means we never got to extend.

panels.title: Steps behind at emission
panels.description: Base-builder submissions that landed while we were merging. Zero means we emitted against a current base.

panels.title: Value budget at emission
panels.description: Milliseconds of base-builder bid growth our merge had to cover, split by whether we won.

panels.title: Value budget in submissions
panels.description: The same budget counted in base-builder submissions rather than milliseconds.

panels.title: 4. Value extraction — what the merge actually appends
Candidate order screening
panels.description: Every candidate order by outcome. `revert_not_allowed` is expected to dominate and is the prize an ordering-aware merge would target.

panels.title: Candidate order value
panels.description: Priority-fee headroom of each candidate, by screening outcome.

panels.title: Emitted value split
panels.description: Total revenue the merged block produced, and the part that went to the proposer as added value.

panels.title: Merged value stored by the relay
panels.description: Merged proposer value minus the original bid, at the moment the relay stored it.

panels.title: 5. Latency — where the time goes inside the builder
Base age at emission
panels.description: How old the base block was when we emitted, split by whether we won. Staleness only hurts through value drift, but the relay gate is absolute.

panels.title: Emission phases
panels.description: One emission's base age split into phases. `worker_wait` and `to_emit` are queueing; `replay` is compute.

panels.title: Stage latency p50
panels.description: Median cost of each merge stage. `replay_txs` and `emit_finalize` carry almost all of it.

panels.title: Stage latency p99
panels.description: Tail cost of each merge stage.

panels.title: State-root walk size
panels.description: Accounts and storage slots the state-root walk touches. `base` against `total` shows how much of every emission is re-walking unchanged work.

panels.title: Speculative stream offers
panels.description: Whether a newly pooled base reached a builder stream. `refused` and `head_not_ready` are merges we never attempted.

panels.title: 6. Builder to relay — receipt, round trip, simulation
Merged block receipt outcomes
panels.description: What the relay did with each merged block. `stale` means the base was no longer appendable for the current slot.

panels.title: Round trip on the relay clock
panels.description: Relay-side time from forwarding or activating a base block to holding a merged block for it. One clock, so it includes both wire legs and all builder compute.

panels.title: Builder-reported latency
panels.description: The builder's own trace as the relay reads it. `recv_to_finalize` is the headline number: under 200ms is where merging wins.

panels.title: Merged block simulation
panels.description: Simulation results. `failed_builder` disables merging and pages; `failed_infra` does not.

panels.title: Merged payload storage
panels.description: Merged payloads offered to the auctioneer. `not_valuable` means the merge did not beat the bid it was built from.

panels.title: Relay merge trace steps
panels.description: Relay-side handling cost for each merge step.

panels.title: Base block age at the get_header decision
panels.description: Age of the merged bid's base when get_header ran, by outcome. Compare `stale` against `served` to see whether max_merged_bid_age_ms is the binding constraint.

panels.title: get_header decision rate
panels.description: Absolute rate of each get_header outcome.
